evidence: Cic. N. D. 1.44: esse igitur deōs cōnfitendum est
Cic. Top. 27: esse ea dīcō quae cernī tangīque possunt
terms.comment: Latin needs no special verb: esse itself asserts existence (Lewis & Short: “Asserting existence, to be, exist, live”), and then often stands first: sunt quī Propertium mālint, there are people who prefer Propertius (Quint. 10.1.93).

terms.gloss: still exist, be extant (of letters, books, buildings)
evidence: Cic. Off. 2.48: exstant epistulae et Philippī ad Alexandrum
Cic. Acad. 2.84: negās tantam similitūdinem in rērum nātūrā esse
Gai. Inst. 3.97a: rem quae in rērum nātūrā esse nōn potest, velut hippocentaurum

phrases.latin: esse ea dīcō quae cernī tangīque possunt, ut fundum, aedēs, parietem …
phrases.english: by things that exist I mean things that can be seen and touched, like a farm, a house, a wall …
we must admit, then, that the gods exist

phrases.latin: Exstant epistulae et Philippī ad Alexandrum …
phrases.english: There still exist letters of Philip to Alexander …
